subject: Logic
title: Veil of Ignorance
description: A short lesson to help you apply Veil of Ignorance.

hook.text: Design a society—but you don't know if you'll be rich or poor, healthy or sick, powerful or powerless.

buildup.text: John Rawls proposed the veil of ignorance in 1971 as a test for fair social rules.

discovery.text: Behind the veil, self-interest becomes fairness. You'd protect the worst-off because you might be them.

twist.text: Critics say it's unrealistic—nobody can truly forget their identity. Rawls says that's the whole point.

climax.text: The experiment doesn't solve justice—it reveals what fairness looks like when stripped of personal advantage.

punchline.text: Fair rules come from forgetting who you are.

quiz.question: What does the veil of ignorance test?
options: Whether social rules are fair when designed without knowledge of one's position
